title: Transport of supported-section kernels for Cartier-related blowups
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Z\subseteq S$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] with finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ [pqf-def-coherent], and let $D\subseteq S$ have an effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal J$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Then $\mathcal J$ is invertible and $\mathcal I\mathcal J$ is finite-type quasi-coherent. Put $Z_D=V(\mathcal I\mathcal J)$, let $b:S'\to S$ and $b_D:S'_D\to S$ be the blowups in $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I\mathcal J$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], and fix the isomorphism $\varphi:S'_D\cong S'$ over $S$ of [lemma-nagata-blowup-invertible-factor]. For a morphism $f:X\to S$ and a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, put $T=X\times_SS'$, $T_D=X\times_SS'_D$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $p:T\to X$, $q:T\to S'$, and $p_D:T_D\to X$. The induced isomorphism $\alpha=\mathrm{id}_X\times_S\varphi:T_D\cong T$ has $p\alpha=p_D$, and the induced module-pullback identification $\alpha^*p^*\mathcal F\cong p_D^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] transports the two strict-transform quotient kernels [def-trf-module-strict-transform] to quasi-coherent submodules $\mathcal K,\mathcal K_D\subseteq p^*\mathcal F$ with the following descriptions, as submodules including their inclusions: for every open $V\subseteq T$,
$$\mathcal K(V)=\{s\in(p^*\mathcal F)(V):s|_{V\setminus q^{-1}b^{-1}(Z)}=0\},\qquad
\mathcal K_D(V)=\{s\in(p^*\mathcal F)(V):s|_{V\setminus q^{-1}b^{-1}(Z\cup D)}=0\}.$$
Here $Z\cup D$ denotes the union of underlying closed subsets. No absence of sections supported on $f^{-1}(D)$ is assumed.

proof.text: The hypothesis already supplies J.IsInvertible. First identify each ideal module with the kernel of O_S to the direct image of the structure sheaf of its closed subscheme. Quasi-coherence of kernels and qcqs pushforward gives quasi-coherence of every ideal module. On each affine open, finite_sections_of_finiteType and the range formula for toModulesι turn the finite-type module hypothesis on I into finite generation of I.ideal. The regular-principal neighbourhoods supplied by hJ make J locally finitely generated; ofFiniteTypeOn.iSup glues this over the cover. Products of finitely generated ideals are finitely generated, and isFiniteType_toModules_sheaf gives finite type of (I * J).toModules. The product support is the union by IdealSheafData.support_mul.

source.place: Divisors, Tag 080H, product centre; Properties, Tags 01PB and 01PG; Schemes, Tags 01IC and 01LC.

proof.text: Use the specified isomorphism φ over S to form the canonical fibre-product map a = pullback.map id φ.hom id. All three component maps are isomorphisms, so a is an isomorphism. Its first projection is p_D by pullback.map_fst. Choose α = asIso a, and choose θ to be exactly tensorPullbackSectionComp.symm followed by the prescribed eqToIso of the first-projection equality. No new blowup comparison is needed, since φ and its equation are hypotheses.

Apply moduleStrictTransform_properties to I and to I * J. Its quasi-coherent-kernel clause gives quasi-coherence of both actual restriction kernels. For any module H and open U, range_map_kernelι identifies the image of the kernel inclusion with sections killed by the open restriction unit; restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app and image_preimage_eq_opensRange_inf identify this with restriction to V intersect U.

source.place: Divisors, Tag 080D (1); Sheaves of Modules, Tag 01AH.

proof.text: For the isomorphism α, write L = tensorPullback α.hom and R = pushforward α.hom. Pushforward along α.inv and R are inverse equivalences, by the identity and composition comparisons. Hence the unit and counit of the normalized tensor adjunction are isomorphisms. Put c = unit_H followed by R(θ), K = the product-centre restriction kernel, KD = R(K), and ιD = R(kernel.ι) followed by c.inv. The map is mono. Set eD equal to the counit at K. Counit naturality and the left triangle identity prove L(ιD) followed by θ equals eD followed by the product-centre kernel inclusion.

source.place: Sheaves, Tags 0095, 0096 and 0097, specialized to inverse ringed-space isomorphisms.

proof.text: Set U equal to the inverse image on the original fibre product of the complement of I.support union J.support. The two pullback projection equalities and support_mul identify α inverse image U with moduleStrictTransformOpen f (I * J). On any V, the equation ιD followed by c.hom = R(kernel.ι) identifies its range with product-kernel sections on α inverse image V. Apply the section-kernel formula of step 3 there. Naturality of c along V intersect U to V identifies restriction of c(s) with c applied to restriction of s. Since c is an isomorphism on sections, that vanishes exactly when the restriction of s vanishes. Apply step 3 also to the original centre to obtain the first displayed formula.

source.place: Divisors, Tag 080H, the geometric identification preceding the affine torsion calculation; Sheaves, Tag 0095.

proof.text: The scheme isomorphism α.hom is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The product-centre kernel K is quasi-coherent by step 3, so qcqs pushforward gives quasi-coherence of KD = R(K). Together with the original-kernel clause from step 3, this proves all required quasi-coherence assertions. The constructions never identify the two kernels and use no torsion hypothesis on F.

Step checks: (1) on a local cover J=(x) with x regular, so multiplication by x is a sheaf isomorphism I to IJ, giving finite type and quasi-coherence, and the prime argument gives |Z_D|=|Z|∪|D|. (2) alpha=id×φ is a valid induced map because φ is over S; its inverse comes from φ⁻¹, and θ comes from the composition isomorphism, with no flatness used. (3) The kernel lemma is applied to both centres, whose finite-type hypotheses hold; fp=bq gives the first formula. (4) The transport along a homeomorphism and along a ring-sheaf isomorphism is an elementary specialization of the pullback definition, so I accept elementary:true. (5) The set identity holds via fp_D=fpα=bqα, and zero restriction transfers because c_{V°} is injective. (6) β^*L_D is quasi-coherent and isomorphic to K_D. Edge cases: with I=O_S, D=V(x), F=O_D the formulas give K=0 and K_D=F, correctly showing the kernels differ without the torsion hypothesis; I=0 is vacuous; D empty gives K=K_D. No duplicates: supported-kernel-blowup-charts is an affine chart description, sheaf-kernel covers a single centre, and the affine torsion comparison is left to its own node.
